findings.where: First screen, the photograph and the ground behind it (desktop and phone); the same treatment again in the motion sketch's preview frame
findings.fault: The direction is 'Mark at work': a full-bleed photograph of him speaking, with his line set over the calm side of that photograph. What is built is something else. The backdrop has been keyed out to a flat slate field and Mark is a cut-out head and shoulders on it. Nothing shows he is speaking: no lectern, no room, no light, only the tip of a microphone. So the first screen reads as a portrait on a dark field, which is the v4 dark-ground and v6 portrait levers. The lever that should set v7 apart is missing.
findings.who_objects: The founder judges the first screens of seven tiles side by side. A v7 that looks like v4 with a portrait gives the round no real 'at work' direction to choose or reject. Mark would also lose the one tile meant to show him in action as an advisor, not posed.

findings.where: First screen, desktop: the photograph against Mark's line and the action
findings.fault: The face is cropped very close and stands about 700 px tall, nearly the height of the screen. Seen at a squint, the giant face wins over the large serif line and over 'Write to me directly'. The reading order goes face, then line, then action, and the face reads larger than life, like a campaign poster.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer arriving from LinkedIn should take in the message and the way to reach him. A looming close-up makes the first impression that of a politician's poster, not the refined, measured advisor the brief asks for.

findings.where: First screen, top bar: 'Mark M. Moseley' beside the MMM Infra mark (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The founder's test says his name leads, with the logo beside it. Here the name is small, light text, while the white mark beside it is larger and heavier, so the eye lands on the firm's logo first.
findings.who_objects: The founder and Mark: the brand sheet (§5) says the individual is the brand, not the firm. A logo that outweighs the name tips the bar back towards 'the firm is the brand'.

findings.where: Phone first screen: the bottom of the photograph against the heading
findings.fault: The heading starts on top of Mark's chin and neck. The photograph fades out under the first line, so the face and the words collide instead of sitting as two separate parts.
findings.who_objects: A visitor on a phone sees his line printed across his face. It looks crowded and unfinished on the screen the founder judges first.

findings.where: Article specimen: the body paragraphs, the subhead, the three-item numbered list and the closing line (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: Long reading text is set centred. Every line starts in a different place, and the numbered list breaks apart: items 2 and 3 sit far from their numbers, and their wrapped lines are centred under them. The specimen exists to show the rhythm holding when Angélique adds a list and a subhead. Instead the list is the part that visibly falls apart, while the side note claims the rhythm holds.
findings.who_objects: Readers of Mark's articles, who are development-bank and government staff reading long arguments: centred paragraphs are slow and tiring to read. The founder too, since the brief names the article specimen as the product and asks it to prove the look survives Angélique's content.

findings.where: Below the fold, the section labels: 'PALETTE' (tracked capitals), 'Type pair' and 'Motion sketch' (small bold sans), 'Texture' (large italic serif), 'An article page' (small bold sans)
findings.fault: The sections are parallel, but each is introduced in a different style, so they don't read as one series. 'Texture' looks like a heading of a higher rank than the rest. 'PALETTE' is set in tracked capitals, which the tile's own type note rules out ('Sentence case, never tracked capitals').
findings.who_objects: The founder, reading the specimen parts as one system: mixed label styles make the tile look unresolved, and the tile breaks its own stated rule.

findings.where: First screen, the lede and the action; the page as a whole
findings.fault: Nothing near the action shows evidence of his work. There is no named body, place or year, no newest talk with its venue, and no regions of his work. The lede says only that he advises 'multilateral development banks, development agencies and governments'. A visitor is asked to write to him with nothing on hand to check.
findings.who_objects: Procurement-minded staff at a development bank, who judge an advisor by relevant work by project kind and region. Without one checkable specific near the address, writing to him is a leap of faith (first-visit trust items 3, 6 and 13).
